question.text: Can the merchant banker or its associates subscribe to a Qualified Institutional Placement (QIP)?

answer.text: Yes, they can subscribe like any other QIB
Yes, but only up to 5% of the issue size
Yes, but only with prior SEBI approval
No, the merchant banker and its associates cannot subscribe to a QIP

explanation.text: The Logic: The SEBI (ICDR) framework places strict conflict-of-interest restrictions on merchant bankers managing a QIP. The merchant banker and its associates are precluded from subscribing to the QIP that they are managing, so that the issue manager remains independent in pricing recommendations and allocation decisions and the QIP genuinely represents arms-length participation by QIBs. The Trap: "Subscribe like any other QIB" ignores the structural conflict between managing the issue and subscribing to it. "Up to 5% of the issue size" is a plausible-sounding partial carve-out, but the prohibition is not framed as a percentage cap. "With prior SEBI approval" suggests a discretionary exemption that does not exist for the merchant banker-as-subscriber to its own QIP. Note: The cited NISM Series IX Merchant Banking workbook pages restrict lead managers and syndicate members from subscribing to a book-built public issue (except to meet underwriting obligations) but do not state an absolute prohibition on merchant bankers and associates subscribing to a QIP. The phrasing above is given as general SEBI (ICDR) regulatory framing for QIP conflicts of interest, not as a workbook-page citation.
